question: Should OpenClaw support `sandbox.mode: "needed"` as a durable public mode that keeps chat direct but activates sandbox isolation only for sandbox-bound tools?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally additive and documented, but it creates a new security and availability contract that cannot be selected solely by code correctness or tests.

options.title: Accept the public mode
options.body: Endorse `needed` as an additive supported configuration mode, subject to a refreshed merge review and the existing fail-closed execution boundary.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep the outage fix but limit it to an explicitly approved existing configuration or owner-specific path instead of adding a durable global mode.

options.title: Pause for sandbox design
options.body: Defer the PR until maintainers decide whether selective tool activation should be generalized with the related sandbox design work.

recommendation.title: Accept the public mode
recommendation.body: Endorse `needed` as an additive supported configuration mode, subject to a refreshed merge review and the existing fail-closed execution boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the intended interaction of the proposed mode with the final proof and affected execution paths; a core sandbox owner should make the product decision.
